name: Taipei
summary: Taipei combines accessible temples, major art collections and easy evening food walks. Put Xinyi and Elephant Mountain together, and save a separate half day for the National Palace Museum.
seasonNote: Autumn is often comfortable; summer is hot and humid with typhoon disruption possible.
arrival: Taoyuan Airport MRT links the airport and Taipei Main Station; choose express or commuter service to suit your stop.
gettingAround: Use MRT plus an EasyCard; the museum needs a bus or taxi connection.
cashTip: Carry NT dollars for night markets and small food stalls; many shops accept cards.
foodTip: Order several small snacks across stalls; pepper buns, beef noodles and oyster omelettes are common choices.
buyTip: Look for tea, pineapple cakes and stationery; check tea origin and packed-food import rules.
baseArea: Taipei Main Station or Zhongshan for convenient connections.

items.name: Le Palais
items.summary: Taipei’s three-star Cantonese restaurant on the 17th floor of the Palais de Chine, known for roast meats and dim sum.
items.expect: A long tasting-menu meal. Deposits, cancellation fees and smart-casual dress codes are common at this level.
items.tip: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.

whyVisit: Taipei’s three-star Cantonese restaurant on the 17th floor of the Palais de Chine, known for roast meats and dim sum.
The MICHELIN Guide awards it Three MICHELIN Stars (exceptional cuisine), the guide’s highest award.
visitFlow: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
Share allergies and dietary needs when booking; tasting menus are hard to change on the night.
Allow about three hours and plan a taxi or short walk back.
items.tradeoffs: Among the most expensive meals of a trip, and tables can sell out weeks or months ahead. Menus are set by the kitchen.
